mainEntity.name: What is the difference between selective demolition and a full interior gut?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full gut strips an entire space down to exterior framing or foundation, while selective demolition removes only chosen elements such as a single partition wall, kitchen cabinets, or specific flooring. The main tradeoff involves budget and scope: selective demolition costs less and allows other areas of a property to remain usable, but it requires greater labor precision and strict dust isolation to prevent cross-contamination into adjacent living or commercial spaces.
acceptedAnswer.description: Selective demolition targets only specified materials while protecting adjacent areas. A full gut strips the entire room or building interior down to bare structural studs.
